newsitem.title: GERMANY: Netanyahu phones Arafat, urges end to clashes.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu phones Arafat, urges end to clashes.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu telephoned Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Thursday and urged him to take "strident action" to calm tension raised by Israel's opening of a controversial archaeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem, Netanyahu's spokesman said.
"The prime minister telephoned Arafat on the importance of calming the situation," spokesman Shai Bazak told reporters aboard Netanyahu's plane on its way from Hanover to Bonn airport.
"Netanyahu made it clear to him that strident action must be taken by the Palestinian authority to calm events that are harming the peace process."

Netanyahu, who came to power 100 days ago on a promise to bolster Israeli security, decided earlier to cut short his visit to Germany by several hours on Thursday so he could return home to deal with the violence.
Fifteen Palestinians have been killed in two days of clashes with Israeli forces over Israeli policy in Jerusalem, holy to Moslems and Jews.
On Tuesday Israel opened a tunnel in the old walled city, which Palestinians said violated a religious and political status quo.
"Arafat agreed with him and said he had already taken action in the field to calm things down," Bazak said.
"Netanyahu told him it was Israel's policy not to harm holy places and therefore there was no basis for the accusations that have been made," Bazak said.
Bazak quoted Netanyahu as telling Arafat: "After things calm we should work together to advance the peace process according to agreed guidelines".
Bazak said that after Netanyahu returns to Jerusalem later on Thursday Israel's security cabinet would convene in the evening.
Netanyahu left Paris for Germany on Thursday morning insisting he would complete a European tour despite the crisis.

But on the road to Bergen-Belsen from Hanover airport in northern Germany, he was briefed by telephone by Israeli defence officials back home. On basis of their report he decided to cut the trip short, Israeli officials said.
After talks with French President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday the Israeli leaderr said that the violence would probably delay a meeting with Arafat's Palestinian Authority from Thursday until Sunday.
